articles.title: Morphology of the endocranial cavities of Stratiotosuchus maxhechti (Notosuchia, Mesoeucrocodylia) from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil.
articles.authors: Philippe George Azambuja, Paulo Victor Luiz Gomes da Costa Pereira, Athirson de Souza Albuquerque et al.
articles.abstract: Notosuchia is a group of mostly terrestrial crocodylomorphs found predominantly in the Mesozoic of Gondwana. Currently, approximately 30 specimens have been reported from the Bauru Group (Paraná Basin) in southeastern Brazil. Baurusuchidae, a notosuchian group comprising only terrestrial species, is typically recovered from the Late Cretaceous of the Bauru Group and includes Stratiotosuchus maxhechti, the focus of this study. Here, we focus on the holotype, recovered from an outcrop of the Adamantina Formation (Paraná Basin) in São Paulo State. The specimen was subjected to computed tomography (CT) to study its encephalic endocast, paratympanic sinus system, nasal cavities, and associated structures. One of these associated structures, the paranasal sinus system, is similar to those described in the literature for other notosuchians, such as Campinasuchus and Barreirosuchus, with pneumatic structures within the maxilla and jugal, as well as a lacrimal sinus. The olfactory region was present, with a morphology different from that of extant taxa (e.g., dorsoventral flattening of the structure) and more similar to the patterns described for other oreinirostral skulls. Despite the poor preservation of the encephalic endocast, it was possible to identify morphological patterns consistent with those reported in other baurusuchids, namely a sigmoid-shaped encephalon oriented almost horizontally, distinct from that of the extant crocodyliform described herein. The paratympanic sinuses were much more complex than in extant taxa. This structure shows high plasticity within the crocodyliform lineage, probably representing a basal characteristic associated with terrestrial habits that was lost in several lineages, especially in aquatic and semiaquatic forms. The paratympanic sinuses and the development of the olfactory region are possible indicators of the importance of sensory organs in supporting the hypercarnivorous paleoecological role historically interpreted for this taxon in the Late Cretaceous of the Bauru Group.

articles.title: The History of Anatomy Is Not Merely the History of Discovering the Human Body; It Is Also the History of How We Have Come to Know the Human Body.
Cellular composition and morphology of the human nasal epithelium in the superior turbinate.
articles.authors: Daiana Yedgey, Victoria F Low, Maurice A Curtis
articles.abstract: The sense of smell is essential for environmental awareness, food safety, and quality of life, yet it is vulnerable to aging, environmental insults, viruses, and neurological disease. Our understanding of the cellular composition and morphology of the human nasal epithelium is heavily influenced by rodent studies or small biopsies from humans. The human nasal cavity contains three epithelial types: olfactory epithelium (OE), transitional epithelium (TE), and respiratory epithelium (RE). Epithelial types differ in the relative composition of olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) and supporting cells. However, the intact human nasal mucosa has not been studied in detail. Here, we characterized the morphology of tissue from large en bloc specimens (>7 cm3) that included both cranial and facial aspects of the olfactory system of 13 embalmed human cadavers. Using histochemical stains, chromogenic and fluorescent immunohistochemistry with markers targeting cilia, sustentacular cells, basal cells, olfactory neurons, olfactory ensheathing cells, fibroblasts, and cell membranes, we assessed the epithelial morphology and continuity from OE through TE to RE. A custom image-analysis pipeline was developed to quantify epithelial thickness and delineate the epithelial subtypes. Our findings demonstrate distinct cellular compositions and structural organization across OE, TE, and RE, confirm variable OE thickness compared with RE, and highlight complex epithelial transitions not captured in small biopsies. This work provides an integrated anatomical and molecular characterization of the human nasal epithelium across its full anatomical extent, establishing a foundational reference for the study of aging, disease, and olfactory dysfunction.

articles.title: A new specimen of Pterygornis dapingfangensis (Aves: Enantiornithes) with implications for early avian cranial morphology.
articles.authors: Min Wang, Zhiheng Li, Zhonghe Zhou
articles.abstract: Disarticulated fossil remains reveal critical anatomical details that are often obscured by the skeletal overlap and taphonomic flattening typical of articulated Mesozoic birds. Here, we report a nearly complete, fully disarticulated enantiornithine bird from the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation, northeastern China. The new specimen, which is referrable to Pterygornis dapingfangensis, reveals previously unknown morphologies and corroborates the presence of a fully fused pelvis in this species. Exquisitely preserved cranial elements demonstrate an ancestral non-avian theropod palatal architecture, characterized by well-developed basipterygoid processes, an elongate vomer bearing a broad premaxillary ramus, and a robust pterygoid with a caudally bifurcated quadrate ramus. This plesiomorphic palate morphology reinforces growing evidence that enantiornithines retained an akinetic skull, suggesting that the enantiornithine cranium was generally evolutionarily conservative.

articles.title: Qualitative and quantitative characterisation of smooth muscle in the human ​common bile duct.
articles.authors: Aryan K Sharma, Jaimin P Chauhan, Abed M Zaitoun et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The distribution and abundance of smooth muscle within the human common bile duct (CBD) remain incompletely characterised, with previous studies relying predominantly on qualitative assessment. This study aimed to characterise smooth-muscle architecture within the human ​CBD using complementary qualitative assessment and semi-automated quantitative digital image analysis. METHODS: ​CBD specimens from 106 pancreaticoduodenectomies and 3 total pancreatectomies were stained for desmin, smooth muscle actin (SMA) and calretinin and analysed using QuPath ( https://qupath.github.io ). RESULTS: Desmin-positive smooth muscle was identified in all specimens and was predominantly scattered (44.0%) or interrupted (26.6%), while focal (25.7%) and continuous circumferential (3.7%) patterns were less frequent. Median desmin-positive area was 1.86% (IQR 1.17-2.79%), compared with 33.55% (IQR 25.96-43.54%) for SMA. Qualitative desmin classification demonstrated moderate concordance with quantitative desmin-positive area (ρ = 0.515, p < 0.001). Smooth-muscle abundance and distribution did not differ significantly between malignant and non-malignant specimens and were not associated with preoperative bilirubin or CBD wall thickness. Malignant specimens demonstrated greater CBD wall thickness than non-malignant specimens despite similar smooth-muscle abundance. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that smooth muscle is consistently identifiable but predominantly sparse and discontinuously distributed within the surgically resected human ​CBD. Semi-automated digital image analysis provides an objective approach to its quantification; however, studies incorporating disease-free controls and functional assessment are required to determine the physiological significance of these findings.

articles.title: Mapping lumbar artery perforators on routine contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic MDCT: distribution, morphology, and a coordinate-based perforator map in a Vietnamese population.
articles.authors: Do Manh Hieu, Nguyen Van Phung
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Imaging data on the lumbar artery perforators (LAPs) are limited and, for Vietnamese subjects, absent. We assessed whether contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic multidetector CT (MDCT) acquired for unrelated indications-with no extra imaging-can characterise LAP distribution and morphology and yield the first coordinate-based perforator map in this population. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic MDCT of 108 subjects (216 hemi-backs) acquired for unrelated indications (256-detector scanner, 0.5 mm reconstruction). On multiplanar, maximum-intensity-projection, and volume-rendered images, each perforator was assigned a source level (LA1-LA4), a diameter at deep-fascia penetration, and cutaneous emergence coordinates on an Oxy system. Within-subject non-independence was handled with the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and cluster-robust regression. RESULTS: Nine hundred seventy-seven perforators were identified. Diameter increased from LA1 to LA4 (LA4-LA1 difference 0.83 mm, 95% CI 0.72-0.95; overall mean 1.98 ± 0.54 mm), whereas number was non-monotonic-lowest at LA2 (n = 121, below LA1 n = 167) and rising sharply to LA3 (n = 247) and LA4 (n = 442). Diameter did not differ by side (p = 0.38) or sex (p = 0.90). The emergence point shifted toward the inter-iliac-crest line from LA1 to LA4 (p < 0.001), forming two paravertebral clusters densest in the lower lumbar region. Clustering was mild (ICC 0.056), leaving conclusions unchanged. CONCLUSION: Routine abdominopelvic MDCT can map lumbar artery perforators without additional imaging. LA3-LA4 are the dominant sources in number and calibre, comparable between sides and sexes; the resulting coordinate-based map-the first for a Vietnamese population-provides a reproducible search window for preoperative localisation, pending intraoperative validation.

articles.title: Anastomosis between an extracranial C1/2-origin left posterior inferior cerebellar artery and the V4 segment of the vertebral artery diagnosed by magnetic resonance angiography.
articles.authors: Atsumasa Toda, Akira Uchino, Yoko Usami et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe a case of a congenital anastomosis between the posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA) arising from the vertebral artery (VA) at the extracranial C1/2 level and the V4 segment of the VA, forming a large arterial ring involving the V3-V4 segments. METHODS: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), including magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), was performed in a 64-year-old man presenting with right lower-extremity weakness for evaluation of suspected cerebrovascular disease. MRI was performed using a 3-T scanner, and MRA was performed using the standard three-dimensional time-of-flight technique. RESULTS: MRI revealed no evidence of acute cerebral infarction. MRA demonstrated that the left PICA originated from the extracranial VA at the C1/2 level. A short but large anastomotic artery was identified between the left PICA and the V4 segment of the left VA, forming a large arterial ring involving the V3-V4 segments. The right VA and right PICA were normal in appearance. Other findings included a small aneurysm of the right internal carotid artery (ICA) and stenosis of the left ICA at its origin. CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of an anastomosis between an extracranial C1/2-origin PICA and the V4 segment of the VA diagnosed by MRA. Although a tiny anastomosis between these arteries may be detected by catheter angiography or cadaveric dissection, it may not be visualized on MRA because of its limited spatial resolution. In the event of occlusion of one channel of the arterial ring, the other channel and the anastomotic artery may serve as important collateral pathways.

articles.title: Phase-Specific Lower-Limb Kinematics and Muscle Activity During 180° Turning in Post-Stroke Hemiplegia: Distinct Reorganization Across Joints and Muscles.
articles.authors: Haochen Tian, Jiaxin Wang, Lingling Chen et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Turning requires phase-specific adjustments in lower-limb motion and muscle activity, yet how these adjustments are altered after stroke remains incompletely understood. This study examined sagittal-plane kinematics and neuromuscular activity across the approach (AP), turning (TP), and departure (DP) phases of a 180° turn in participants with post-stroke hemiplegia (SP). METHODS: Twelve SP and 12 age-matched healthy participants (HP) performed affected-side (AS) and unaffected-side (US) 180° turns. Hip, knee, and ankle kinematics and surface electromyography (sEMG) from eight lower-limb muscles were recorded. AP, TP, and DP were represented by complete gait cycles selected using pelvic-rotation landmarks. sEMG amplitudes were normalized to within-task references, and two ankle coactivation indices (CCI) were calculated. Outcomes were analyzed using a unified 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 mixed analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Group, Direction, Limb, and Phase as factors. RESULTS: HP showed joint-specific phase modulation, particularly at the hip and ankle. In SP, hip modulation was attenuated, while swing-phase knee flexion and knee range of motion (ROM) were markedly reduced. Peak ankle plantarflexion was lower in SP. Muscle activity changes were also muscle- and condition-specific. At the ankle, higher normalized activity in selected muscles coexisted with lower tibialis anterior-medial gastrocnemius (TA-MG) CCI. Turning direction modified selected outcomes through its interaction with leg role, but US turning did not systematically amplify post-stroke abnormalities. SIGNIFICANCE: Sagittal-plane joint motion and accompanying muscle activity during post-stroke 180° turning show selective attenuation and reorganization of phase-dependent patterns rather than a uniform loss of modulation. Analyzing AP, TP, and DP separately reveals altered phase modulation alongside reductions in knee motion that persist across the turning sequence.

articles.title: Endurance Exercise Training Before Myocardial Infarction Reduces Decline of Myocardial Function in Old Mice.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Cajetan Immanuel Lang, Robert Schenke, Sinan Schlüter et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pre-infarction endurance training reduces scar formation and adverse cardiac remodeling in rodents; however, evidence is largely restricted to young animals. Whether these benefits extend to aged individuals, the population most affected by myocardial infarction (MI), remains unclear. METHODS: We investigated the effects of 6 weeks of endurance exercise training prior to MI in aged mice (20 months). C57BL/6 mice were randomized to exercise (EX-MI, n=11; treadmill running 30 min/day, 5 days/week) or sedentary conditions (SED-MI, n=12). MI was induced by permanent ligation of the left anterior descending artery. FDG PET imaging was performed on days 5 and 7 post MI, and cardiac structure and function were evaluated by MRI at day 28. Histological analyses were performed ex vivo. RESULTS: Exercise training resulted in smaller and thicker infarct scars compared with sedentary controls. Despite similar lef t ventricular dilation, EX-MI mice showed significantly improved systolic function, with higher ejection fraction and stroke volume. This was supported by enhanced global longitudinal and radial strain rates. Likewise, regional deformation analysis demonstrated higher circumferential and radial strain within the scar. FDG uptake was increased in the infarct region at day 7. Additionally, remote myocardium was thicker and exhibited greater radial deformation in exercised animals. CONCLUSIONS: Our study shows that short time endurance exercise training in older mice prior to acute MI reduces post-MI left ventricular remodeling, scar size, and scar thinning. Myocardial contractility in both the remote and infarct areas were preserved by endurance training, potentially reflecting an enhanced compensatory capacity induced by pre-infarction exercise training.

articles.title: Combined resistance and aerobic exercise in chronic kidney disease: An exploratory study of physical activity as a moderator of adaptations.
articles.authors: Jared M Gollie, Alice S Ryan, Michael O Harris-Love et al.
articles.abstract: Physical inactivity is common in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and might contribute to impaired skeletal muscle and physical function. Whether habitual physical activity (PA) influences adaptation to structured exercise in CKD remains unclear. We examined the effects of 6 weeks of combined flywheel resistance and aerobic exercise (FRE+AE) on neuromuscular and physical function and explored whether baseline self-reported PA moderated treatment response in older male Veterans with stages 3-4 CKD. Twenty-four participants were randomized to FRE+AE (n = 12) or health education (EDU; n = 12). Outcomes included vastus lateralis (VL MT) and rectus femoris (RF MT) muscle thickness, maximal voluntary isometric torque (MVIT), isokinetic knee-extensor power at 60° s- 1 and 180° s- 1, gait speed (GS), five-repetition sit-to-stand (STS) and timed up and go (TUG). Intervention effects were evaluated using baseline-adjusted linear regression, and baseline PA was examined as a continuous moderator. At 6 weeks, FRE+AE resulted in greater VL MT than EDU (adjusted difference, 3.31 mm; 95% confidence interval, 0.91-5.71; P = 0.010) and greater GS (0.17 m s- 1; 95% confidence interval, 0.07-0.26; P = 0.002). Treatment effects for RF MT (2.09 mm; P = 0.051) and isokinetic power at 180° s- 1 (28 W; P = 0.060) favoured FRE+AE but were not statistically significant after controlling for multiple comparisons. No clear treatment effects were observed for MVIT, power at 60° s- 1, STS or TUG. Baseline PA did not moderate treatment effects across outcomes. These findings demonstrate that short-term FRE+AE can improve VL MT and GS in older male Veterans with moderate-to-advanced CKD, whereas baseline habitual self-reported PA did not explain variation in treatment responsiveness.

articles.title: Validity of a Consumer-Grade Bioelectrical Impedance Device for Body Composition Assessment Compared with a Three-Compartment Model in Recreationally Active Adults.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Patrick G Saracino, Hannah K Eberhardt, Cecilia D Salas et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to validate a consumer multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance device against a 3-compartment (3C) model in recreationally active adults. Following an overnight fast and abstention from caffeine (12 h), alcohol (24 h), and strenuous exercise (24 h), participants underwent body composition assessment using a consumer multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance device (BIAH30; InBody Dial H30). A criterion 3C model was derived from body mass, body volume via air displacement plethysmography, and total body water via a validated multi-frequency bioelectrical impedance device. Fifty-five recreationally active participants (29M/26F; 22±4 years, 170.5±8.2 cm; 70.6±10.5 kg; 24.2±2.6 kg·m⁻²) completed the study. BF% (21.7±7.8% vs 19.9±7.8%) and FM (15.3±5.8 vs 14.0±5.8 kg) were higher with BIAH30 compared to 3C (p < 0.001), whereas FFM (55.5±10.6 vs 56.7±10.4 kg) was lower (p < 0.001). Bland-Altman analysis indicated mean biases of 1.9% (95% LOA: -4.0 to 7.7%), 1.3 kg (95% LOA: -2.7 to 5.3 kg), and -1.2 kg (95% LOA: -5.1 to 2.8 kg) for BF%, FM, and FFM, respectively, with no proportional bias. Lin's concordance correlation coefficient indicated moderate to strong agreement (CCC: 0.90-0.98). In conclusion, the InBody H30 demonstrated significant differences in BF%, FM, and FFM relative to 3C. Mean bias was small, no proportional bias was observed, and agreement was moderate to strong. However, 95% limits of agreement were wide, indicating notable individual variability. While the H30 may serve as a practical, low-cost option for group-level estimates or longitudinal tracking, it should not be considered interchangeable with multi-compartment models for precise individual-level measurement.

articles.title: Bone Health in Female Athletes Using Hormonal Contraceptives.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Lauren A Burt, Kelly Drager, Emily Smith-Bregeda et al.
articles.abstract: The objectives of this study were to (1) report the prevalence and type of hormonal contraception (HC) use among Canadian elite and world-class athletes and (2) investigate associations between current HC use and bone density, microarchitecture and strength, accounting for sport type (endurance vs. non-endurance). Participants included 61 high performance athletes, mean age 24 years. Endurance-based sport affiliations include long-track speed skating (n=16), cross-country skiing (n=13) and biathlon (n=9). Non-endurance sports were ski cross (n=7), figure skating (n=6), luge (n=4), ski jumping (n=4), and combat sports (n=2). High-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography scans of the radius and tibia were acquired and outcome measures included bone mineral density, microarchitecture, geometry and bone strength. Questionnaires captured sport affiliation and reproductive health information. Two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed to examine the effects of current HC use (yes/no) and sport type (endurance/non-endurance) on bone variables. HC prevalence was 69% (n=42) and the majority of athletes used progestin only intrauterine devices (IUDs, n=29). No evidence of detrimental effects resulting from HC use was found in this cohort. Although some differences were observed between groups, no interaction effects remained significant after multiple-comparison correction and these findings should be interpreted with caution. Overall, the results do not support clinically meaningful differences in bone health between HC groups. These findings highlight the need for longitudinal research examining the effects of currently prevalent HC methods, particularly IUDs, on overall bone health and strength along with lifetime fracture risk in athletes.

articles.title: Long-term outcomes following non-operative treatment of grade II and III medial collateral ligament injuries with and without concomitant ACL injury.
articles.authors: Jamie S Brown, Anders Isacsson, Jaanika Paemre et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-operative treatment is widely accepted for isolated grade II medial collateral ligament (MCL) injuries. However, optimal management of grade III injuries, particularly those associated with anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, remains controversial. METHODS: A prospective cohort of consecutive acute knee injuries were referred for subacute MRI. Grade II or III MCL injuries on MRI were followed-up with Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), Tegner activity scale (TAS), clinical examination, and radiography at mean 11.5 years in 154 of 202 (76%) patients. RESULTS: KOOS and TAS were not statistically significantly different in patients with MCL grade II compared to MCL grade III injury and MCL grade II compared to MCL grade II/ACL injury. There were no statistically significant differences in KOOS after MCL grade II/ACL compared to MCL grade III/ACL injury, however the TAS was lower in the latter (median 4 versus 2, p = 0.038, 95% CI 0-2). There were statistically significant differences in KOOS Sport/recreation, QOL, KOOS4 and TAS after MCL grade III/ACL injury compared to isolated MCL grade III injury (median 75 vs. 90 [p = 0.015, 95% CI 0-30], 75 vs. 88 [p = 0.022, 95% CI 0-25], 81 vs. 88 [p = 0.052, 95% CI 0-17] and 2 vs. 4 [p = 0.014, 95% CI 0-2] respectively). The proportion with radiographic osteoarthritis was 25% after isolated MCL grade II/III and 41% for MCL grade II/III with ACL injury. CONCLUSIONS: With the exception of a lower TAS for MCL grade III/ACL compared to MCL grade II/ACL, non-operatively managed grade III MCL injuries with and without ACL injury had comparable patient-reported and radiographic outcomes compared to their grade II counterparts.

articles.title: Risk factors and efficacy comparison of different treatment methods for cervical spondylotic myelopathy complicated with traumatic central cord syndrome.
articles.authors: Shaosong Sun, Xingchen Zhang, Youlai Yu et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: We aimed to analyze the independent risk factors for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) patients with traumatic central cord syndrome (TCCS). In addition, the short-term and medium-term efficacy of conservative treatment and surgical treatment on patients' neurological function and imaging were compared. METHODS: Total of 182 patients with CSM admitted in our hospital during January 2016 to December 2021 were chosen as the study subjects. They were divided into a complicated group (with TCCS) and a non-complicated group (without TCCS). Influencing factors were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. A nomogram prediction model was constructed based on these factors. Patients with TCCS were divided into a conservative group (n = 30) and a surgical group (n = 38) according to the actual treatment received. Changes in the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) score, Spinal Cord Independence Measure III (SCIM-III) score, modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association (mJOA) score, and imaging parameters were compared between the two groups before treatment and at 3 and 6 months after treatment. Subgroup analyses were also performed according to ASIA grade, surgical timing, and surgical approach. Complications and the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) were assessed. RESULTS: Age, positive pathological signs, hand intrinsic muscle score, intramedullary high signal (IMHS) length, degree of spinal cord compression, and degree of spinal canal stenosis were all associated with CSM complicated by TCCS (P < 0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis showed that advanced age (OR = 2.264), high IMHS length (OR = 2.532), high degree of spinal cord compression (OR = 3.438), and high degree of spinal canal stenosis (OR = 3.900) were independent risk factors for CSM complicated by TCCS. And high hand intrinsic muscle score (OR = 0.430) was an independent protective factor (all P < 0.05). A nomogram prediction model was constructed based on the above five factors. At 3 months after treatment, the improvements in ASIA sensory and motor scores, SCIM-III score, mJOA score, intervertebral space height, and cervical lordosis angle in the surgical group were significantly greater than those in the conservative group (all P < 0.05), and the differences reached the MCID threshold. At 6 months after treatment, no significant differences were observed in any indicators between the two groups (all P > 0.05). Subgroup analysis by ASIA grade showed that in the B/C grade subgroup, the improvement in ASIA motor score at 3 months was greater in the surgical group than in the conservative group (P = 0.038). No significant differences in neurological improvement were found between the surgical timing subgroups or between the surgical approach subgroups. There was no significant difference in the incidence of complications between the two groups (P > 0.05), and no severe complications were observed in either group. CONCLUSION: Advanced age, low hand intrinsic muscle score, high IMHS length, high degree of spinal cord compression, and high degree of spinal canal stenosis are independent risk factors for CSM complicated by TCCS. The nomogram provides a visual tool for clinical risk screening. Surgical treatment can significantly promote early (3-month) recovery of neurological function and imaging structure compared with conservative treatment, offering a distinct advantage in accelerating rehabilitation. However, the efficacy of the two treatment modalities converges at 6 months.

articles.title: Postprandial response prediction after high-carbohydrate and high-fat standardised meals using global, local, and phenotypic scores.
articles.authors: F M Del Razo-Olvera, A T Arias-Marroquín, A Huerta-Chagoya et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Metabolic risk is assessed almost entirely from fasting samples, although adults spend most waking hours postprandially. We tested whether fasting-derived polygenic and phenotypic scores predict the postprandial excursion itself. SUBJECTS/METHODS: In a hypothesis-generating physiological study, 96 Mexican adults underwent standardised high-carbohydrate and high-fat meal challenges in random order. We tested a multi-ancestry-derived global polygenic score (gPRS), a four-variant Mexico-specific score (mxPRS) and phenotypic scores against the fasting concentration, the postprandial trajectory and the incremental area under the curve (iAUC). RESULTS: The phenotypic score predicted glucose and insulin trajectories (β = 8.1 mg/dL and 17.5 µU/mL per SD, both p < 0.001) but not glucose iAUC (p = 0.358). The mxPRS predicted triglycerides in both domains (fasting p = 0.027; iAUC β = 2808 mg/dL·min per SD, p = 0.026) and neither glucose nor insulin iAUC. The gPRS predicted no fasting concentration and no iAUC except insulin after carbohydrate, which was unstable. Most variance was unexplained. CONCLUSIONS: These exploratory findings are hypothesis-generating. Ancestry-relevant variants merit further study as predictors of postprandial lipaemia in admixed populations, and accessible phenotypic measurements carry more information about postprandial glucose and insulin than a multi-ancestry genome-wide score.
